title: Composite pattern
idea: The Composite pattern lets you treat a single object and a tree of objects the same way, through one shared interface that groups implement by delegating to children.

analogy.text: A shipping pallet holds cartons, cartons hold boxes. Ask any of them its weight and it answers, adding up whatever is inside.
analogy.breaks: A pallet cannot sit inside itself; code must forbid that cycle explicitly.

points: Component is the shared interface; a leaf answers alone, a composite asks its children.
Recursion replaces type checks: callers never ask whether an item is a group.
AWT uses it: `java.awt.Container` is a `Component` that holds other components.
Use it for genuine part-whole trees; a flat list needs no composite.

hero.title: One price call walks the tree

steps.caption: The caller asks the kit for its price. The caller holds only a `CatalogItem` and does not know it is a bundle.
The kit loops over its children. The first child is itself a bundle, so a new frame opens.
The desk set asks the Desk, a leaf. A leaf has no loop: it returns its own price.
The Desk frame pops, returning its price to the desk set. The Chair is called and returns the same way.
The desk set sums both children, applies its own 5% and returns one number.
Back in the kit's loop, the Monitor leaf answers.
The Monitor frame pops and its price returns to the kit.
The kit sums its two children and applies 10%. Same code at every depth, no type checks.

code.title: The problem: type checks
code.caption: No shared interface: the pricing code must test types and hard-code how deep bundles nest.

walk.text: `Product` and `Bundle` share no type, so a bundle stores a `List<Object>`.
Every caller needs an `instanceof` ladder, and must change when a new item type appears.
Nested bundles get one hand-written level. Their discount is ignored, and deeper bundles vanish.
The desk set is right, the kit overcharges, and the team pack loses both desk sets.
Bundles of bundles are normal in catalogues. A fixed depth will always be too small.

code.title: The fix: a composite
code.caption: Products and bundles share `CatalogItem`; a bundle delegates to its children at any depth.

walk.text: The component interface. `contains` has a leaf-friendly default, so only the composite overrides it.
The leaf is an immutable record that validates its price and answers from its own data.
The composite's price is its children's sum, discounted. Each child may be a leaf or another bundle.
`add` rejects null and any item that already contains this bundle, which would recurse forever.
`contains` walks the subtree, using the same recursion as pricing.
`print` shows the tree: each level indents its children and repeats the same call.
The same kit appears twice under the team pack, and a cycle attempt fails fast.

pitfalls: A cycle (a bundle inside itself) makes `pricePence` overflow the stack; check `contains` in `add`.
`add` on the component makes leaves throw at runtime; prefer the composite for type safety.
Returning the live children list lets callers bypass validation; return `List.copyOf` instead.

quiz.q: Using the classes from the fix, what does this print?
quiz.why: Each level applies its own discount to its children's total. `inner` returns 200, then `outer` halves that again.

takeaway: Leaves answer for themselves; composites ask their children and combine.
